text: The instruction is composed here and the partner and partner_instruction rows stay with the partner-management service: the firm is read on its contract, the instruction is requested on the same contract with the pack reference set and answered with the instruction reference, instructed_at and due_at, and this service writes no business row, no document and no partner field. The pack of the instruction is a set of document references read on API-P5-002, and the two provided operations remain API-S4-002 and API-S4-003 of the legacy endpoints block.
why: The legacy data table names partner and partner_instruction, but the ownership rows of rwb-litigation name only hearing and legal_action, the pack items are P5's, and no source names an operation of the partner portal; declaring those rows here would copy two services' facts into this schema, and inventing an operation would widen the five owned operations of the service.
read: Context pack ownership rows of S4 and Architecture v5 slides 4, 8 and 10; TSD S4 T3.1, T5.2 and T-A.1; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 rows FEAT-LIT-09 and FEAT-PRM-02; FSD S4 A2.9; legacy RWB-E5-009 data and endpoints tables.
confirm: Solution architect of S4 with the S9 and P5 architects for the consumed contracts
impact: If S4 turns out to own the instruction row, this story gains one table, one migration and a write path; the rules, the clock and the case answer do not change.

text: FIRM_MATCHED, FIRM_NOMINATED and FIRM_BREACHED_SLA are read as the names of workflow signals and state-machine events, not as Kafka subscriptions: the firm arrives on the workflow signal of the selection step, the firm facts are read on the partner contract, the case read and the case-stage answer travel on the rwb-case contract, and this legacy key publishes and consumes no event.
why: The Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 names an event per rule, while the ownership rows give rwb-litigation zero events, the FSD declares no background event and DP-09 is not in the pattern set; a consumer or a producer invented here would put a topic, an inbox and an event catalogue entry into a service the ownership map gives none.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-24, R-LIT-26 and R-LIT-28; context pack ownership rows; FSD S4 A2.9.4.4; TSD S4 T4, T5.2 and T5.3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and DP-14.
applied_in: RWB-S4-E5009-APP sections 2, 4, 12.3, 12.4, 12.5, 13; RWB-S4-E5009-CON sections 2, 7 (AC4, AC6), 12.3, 12.4, 12.5, 19; the events keys of both fragments
confirm: Solution architect of S4 with the P3 and S9 architects and the event platform team
impact: If an event is preferred, the key gains a consumed event plus an inbox, DP-09 enters the pattern set and both metadata rows change; the rule evaluation and the clock do not change.

text: The partner clock is one durable timer of LitigationWorkflow of 2 working days started at instructed_at on a working-day calendar read as a versioned reference row; on expiry R-LIT-28 fires, the instruction is marked breached on the partner contract, FIRM_BREACHED_SLA is answered to rwb-case with the partner-and-agency-manager task and the re-selection stays with the firm-selection story. The case-stage timer and the task row stay rwb-case's, requested on the stage outcome.
why: The timer row of the legacy data table is P3's and the pack gives S4 no job but one workflow, while litigation clocks run for months and must survive releases; the working-day calendar and the instruction types have no value in any source, so they cannot be constants and must be reference rows that can be absent.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-24, R-LIT-26 and R-LIT-28; context pack Jobs (0), Workflows (1) and Temporal and Drools slide 7 notes; TSD S4 T3.2, T5.3 and T6; legacy RWB-E5-009 data table (timer DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036); FSD S4 A2.9.3.1 (BR-S4-009).
confirm: Business owner of the partner service levels with the S4, P3 and S9 solution architects
impact: If the clock must be a case-service or partner-service timer, the answer or the request grows a duration field and the workflow drops one timer; if the calendar arrives late, only reference data changes.

text: Both stories trace to FEAT-LIT-09 and to REQ-S4-004, 'A law firm is selected from the panel by rule using panel performance, and instructed through the partner portal', with the reading stated in section 18, and the PRD column stays Pending (C1) until the Epics 3 to 8 PRD adds an identifier for the instruction.
why: The legacy master of RWB-E5-009 and the Epics 3 to 8 specification carry no requirement identifier for this feature and the FSD S4 requirements table names no instruction requirement of its own; writing an identifier by pattern would create a reference no owner approved and no requirement trace can resolve.

impact: The traceability roll-up of the two stories only; no build effect.

text: The LITIGATION package is consumed from rwb-decision as a non-blocking contract with its fake, at its version in force, and the embedded rules runtime stays a service-template capability of the platform. Neither story declares a rule row, a package or a rule version of its own, and the metadata rows of both stories keep Contract dependencies None.
why: The three rules cannot be evaluated without the package, but DP-04 is not in the pattern set of this key and no dependency row exists for its two contracts; authoring the package here would take rule governance away from rwb-decision and duplicating the rows would let the rule and the story drift.
read: Context pack DP table DP-04 and Temporal and Drools slide 11 rule governance block; FSD S4 A2.9.3.1 (BR-S4-009); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-24, R-LIT-26 and R-LIT-28; the metadata rows and pattern sets of both stories.
confirm: P7 rwb-decision architect with the solution architect of S4
impact: If the package read is made a C dependency later, only the Dependency Map and the metadata rows change; the evaluation code and the tests do not.
